common_name: Miss Ruby Loropetalum (Large Reblooming Purple Fringe Flower)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring in well-drained, moderately fertile, slightly acidic soil in full sun to partial shade; Miss Ruby grows larger and more vigorously than most compact loropetalum cultivars and needs room to reach full size.

directions: Plant in well-drained, moderately fertile, slightly acidic soil in full sun to partial shade, giving it the 5–6 foot mature spread it needs to avoid constant shearing. Bred by the U.S. National Arboretum, Miss Ruby is a vigorous, large-growing loropetalum selected for foliage that emerges bright magenta-red and matures to a rich, dark burgundy-purple that holds its color through summer heat better than many older loropetalum cultivars, along with a heavy spring flush of frilly, ribbon-like hot-pink flowers and scattered rebloom into fall. Its larger scale suits it to hedges, screens, and background plantings rather than tight foundation spaces, and it tolerates both full sun (best color) and open shade. Prune, if needed, right after the spring bloom flush to avoid removing next year's flower buds.

common_name: Ruby Snow Loropetalum (Variegated White-Flowered Fringe Flower)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring in well-drained, moderately fertile, slightly acidic soil in full sun to partial shade; variegated foliage color is brightest with a few hours of direct sun.

directions: Plant in well-drained, moderately fertile, slightly acidic soil in full sun to partial shade, and prune out any solid-green reverted shoots as soon as they appear to keep the variegation stable. Ruby Snow is an unusual loropetalum grown as much for its foliage as its flowers, with new leaves emerging burgundy-pink and maturing to green heavily marbled and edged in cream-white, a striking departure from the solid purple or green foliage of most loropetalum cultivars, paired with clean white, ribbon-like spring flowers rather than the typical pink or magenta. Its compact, rounded habit and bright, contrasting foliage make it a strong accent or specimen plant where a bolder color break is wanted among evergreen shrubs. Prune lightly right after spring bloom if shaping is needed, since flower buds set on the current season's growth soon after.
